rationale: validation_status=fail with an uncovered_requirement issue for SR3: the SR3-targeting mutant (condition_negation) inverts the exhaustion guard so that the boundary call at counter==0xFFFFFFFF proceeds with full encryption side effects instead of being blocked, and only sets have_used_max afterward. This genuinely reintroduces nonce reuse at the wraparound boundary (the very defect SR3 is meant to catch: an off-by-one/ordering error in the exhaustion check relative to side effects). The mutant is not equivalent to the golden — it changes observable behavior (the boundary call returns 0 and emits ciphertext instead of erroring). Yet SR3's own check failed to detect this corrupted-but-compiling submission (mutants_detected: 0 of 1 targeting). This means the SR3 check in evaluate.py is not independently probing the pre-side-effect ordering of the exhaustion guard; it likely only exercises the same call sequence already covered by SR1/SR2's checks in a way that happens to still pass under this mutant, or its assertion on the expected success/failure pattern isn't strict enough to catch a one-call-late guard. Since analyzer_status=fail, validation_status=fail, and mutation_score(0.857) is only borderline informative given the uncovered SR3 gap, the case should not be retained as-is. Per the uncovered_requirement rule, root cause is on the evaluation framework, not the mutant.
revision_instructions: SR3's behavioral check in evaluate.py fails to detect a mutant that reorders the exhaustion guard so it fires one call late: the corrupted submission proceeds to perform full encryption (writes ciphertext_out/tag_out and advances/wraps state) on the call at counter==0xFFFFFFFF before ever marking exhaustion, meaning that call returns 0 and produces ciphertext instead of the required nonzero error, and the *next* call reuses counter/nonce 0 successfully. Strengthen the SR3 harness so it does not rely solely on the same call sequence SR1/SR2 already exercise. Concretely: using the AEAD_TEST_COUNTER_START test seam, drive the submission to exactly the call where the counter is at its maximum value for the first time, and assert on that SPECIFIC call (not just some later call) that (a) the return code is nonzero, and (b) ciphertext_out/tag_out sentinel buffers are untouched. Do not only check that a wraparound eventually gets blocked a call or two later — pin the check to the exact boundary call index derived from AEAD_TEST_COUNTER_START, so a guard that fires one call late is observably wrong. This must be graded purely by executing the compiled submission against the pinned interface (compile with g++, run the harness binary, inspect return codes and buffer contents) — never by matching source text, since a correct implementation may structure its exhaustion tracking differently from the reference. The check must FAIL on any submission (mutant or otherwise) that allows even a single extra call to succeed before the boundary is enforced, and must PASS on any implementation that enforces the boundary exactly at the documented call index.
